SpendObserver is an app for keeping track of expenses and income. The app works entirely locally: it requires no internet connection, registration or cloud services.
The app does not share user data with third parties and does not send it over the network. All trackers, records and tags are stored in the device’s memory.

If backup to a Google account is enabled in the device settings, the Android operating system may save the app’s data to that account’s cloud storage. Such backup is performed by the system according to the device settings; the app takes no part in it.

When the app is uninstalled, its data is deleted from the device. To keep the data or move it to another device, it is recommended to export it to a file (menu “⋮” → “%1$s”) and then import it (menu “⋮” → “%2$s”).

string-array.name: faq_trackers_a
string-array.item: A tracker is a separate log with its own records and tags, for example a personal, family or work one. Trackers are independent of each other.
To create a tracker, tap “Add tracker” on the main screen and enter a name. The new tracker opens right away.
A tracker can be renamed or deleted with the ✎ and 🗑 buttons in its row on the main screen, or through the “⋮” menu on the tracker screen. Deleting a tracker deletes all of its records.

resources.string: How do I add, edit or delete a record?

string-array.name: faq_records_a
string-array.item: Open a tracker and tap “Add record”. Choose the record type (“Expense” or “Income”), set the date and the amount, select tags and add a description if needed, then tap “Save”.

Records are grouped by year and month; each group shows its number of records and its total. To edit a record, tap it in the list. A record can be deleted with the 🗑 button at the top of the record form.

resources.string: What are record parts and the receipt total?

string-array.name: faq_parts_a
string-array.item: A record corresponds to a single event, such as one receipt, and may consist of several parts. Each part has its own amount and its own tags. The amount of a record always equals the sum of its parts.
To divide a record, tap “Split into parts” below the amount field. New parts are added with the “+ Part” button; unneeded ones are removed with the ✕ button.

If the total of the receipt is known, enter it in the “Receipt total” field and single out individual parts. The remainder is calculated automatically and becomes the last part. The parts singled out must add up to less than the receipt total.
Two parts of the same record cannot have the same set of tags.

resources.string: How do global tags differ from regular tags?

string-array.name: faq_tag_levels_a
string-array.item: Global tags describe a record as a whole: where or with whom it took place (for example, the name of a shop or of a trip). One tag or none can be selected in the “Global tags” field of the record form; tapping another tag replaces the selected one.
Regular tags describe what the money was spent on or where it came from (for example, “groceries”). They are selected for each part of a record separately.
A tag’s level is chosen when the tag is created and cannot be changed later. A new tag is created with the “+” button in the corresponding field of the record form or on the tracker edit screen.

resources.string: How do I rename or delete a tag?

string-array.name: faq_tag_manage_a
string-array.item: Open a tracker, choose “Edit” in the “⋮” menu and use the ✎ and 🗑 buttons next to the tag. Each tag shows how many records use it.
A deleted tag is removed from all records; the records themselves are kept.

resources.string: How do I use the calculator in the amount field?

string-array.name: faq_calculator_a
string-array.item: The amount field accepts an expression with the operations +, −, × (*) and ÷ (/) and parentheses, for example 120+50/2. The result is shown below the field and saved as the amount.

Multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction, as on any calculator: 120+50/2 = 145. Use parentheses to change the order: (120+50)/2 = 85. Both a dot and a comma are accepted as the decimal separator. The field only takes digits, operation signs and parentheses, and two signs in a row are not possible: a new sign replaces the previous one. The result is rounded to two decimal places and must be greater than zero.

resources.string: How do I use the statistics?

string-array.name: faq_stats_a
string-array.item: Open a tracker and choose “Statistics” in the “⋮” menu. The “−”/“+” switch at the top of the screen selects expenses or income.

The summary shows the number of records, the total for the selected period and the tags of both levels that occur most often and account for the largest amounts. The selection field lets you choose a single tag to view statistics for it alone.

The chart shows amounts or numbers of records (the “Amount”/“Records” switch) by year, month or day. Tapping a bar opens the corresponding year or month; to return to a larger period, use the links in the top row.

resources.string: How do I save data to a file?

string-array.name: faq_export_a
string-array.item: To save all trackers, open the “⋮” menu on the main screen and choose “Save all to file” or “Share all”. To save a single tracker, use “Save to file” or “Share” in the “⋮” menu on the tracker screen.
The data is saved to a JSON file, which can be kept as a backup or used to move the data to another device.

resources.string: How do I load data from a file?

string-array.name: faq_import_a
string-array.item: Open the “⋮” menu on the main screen, choose “Import from file” and select a previously saved file. The trackers contained in the file are listed before the import.

If a tracker with the same name already exists, choose an action: “Copy” adds the tracker from the file under a new name, “Replace” deletes the existing tracker with all its records and loads the tracker from the file.
The file is checked in full before the import. If an error is found, no data is loaded, and the message states where the error is.
